slides.title: Your first Laval plex: 5 rules before you offer
slides.sub: Duplex, triplex or 4-plex: what changes when tenants come with it.

photo.credit: Photo: Jeangagnon, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: Living there changes your down payment
slides.body: Example: a **$700,000 duplex** you live in needs at least **$45,000** down. Confirm with your mortgage broker.

slides.title: The leases come with the building
slides.body: You can't change current leases after you buy. Get every lease and expense record from the seller first.
slides.source: Per Tribunal administratif du logement, October 2026

slides.title: Rent increases follow TAL rules
slides.body: It's a reference, not a cap. Tenants can refuse an increase, and the **TAL** can set the rent.

slides.title: Near the water? Check the flood map

photo.credit: Photo: Laslovarga, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Looking in **Laval-Ouest**, **Îles-Laval** or **Saint-Vincent-de-Paul**? Search the address on Québec's flood zone map first.

slides.title: Run the real costs, not a guess
slides.body: Ask for the actual **Laval tax bills** and utility costs. Then walk through cash flow with your accountant.
